prompt: Pattern A starts at $0$ and adds $2$ each time: $0, 2, 4, 6, \dots$ Pattern B starts at $0$ and adds $4$ each time: $0, 4, 8, 12, \dots$ Each number in Pattern B is ___ the matching number in Pattern A.
hint: Line the patterns up in pairs: $2$ with $4$, $4$ with $8$, $6$ with $12$.

hints.text: Line the patterns up in pairs: $2$ with $4$, $4$ with $8$, $6$ with $12$.
Ask "what do I multiply $2$ by to get $4$?" and check that the same thing works for $4$ and $8$.
Every B number is $2$ times the matching A number.

explanation: $2 \times 2 = 4$, $2 \times 4 = 8$, and $2 \times 6 = 12$ — doubling works every single time.
"$2$ more than" only works for the first pair or two, so it is not the real relationship.
Pattern B is always $2$ times Pattern A.

alternativeExplanations.title: Look at the rules
steps: B adds $4$ each step while A adds $2$ each step.
B is growing twice as fast from the same start, so it stays exactly double.
